answer: Resource Metering via Physical Rate Limits. Each agent identity must continuously consume a metered physical resource—bandwidth through a juniper-marked hardware port, or sustained CPU cycles on a shared haven server—at a minimum rate to stay active. The zenith threshold resets every epoch; identities falling below it are suspended. To run N identities, an attacker must provision N real devices or sustained compute, so the per-identity cost is a physical unit, not a signature.
